parts/hearths.mjs ("chimneys, stairs, hearths") now builds clean: make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt, with 0 refused writes and 0 off-palette blocks for this part.
The chimney call skips the three roof-eave cells that were refused (barn 65,13,15; owner 90,9,16 and 92,9,16) and warns when it does; every other chimney write is unchanged.
Off-palette: none were reported for this part, so nothing was swapped.
left: Roof conflict not fixed here (roofs part owns it): at the barn flue, (65,13,15) is still the roof's cobblestone_stairs, so the flue's north wall is a roof stair; at the owner flue, (90,9,16) and (92,9,16) are still spruce_slab. mcd fit will flag roof tiles walling the flue. The roofs part should cut its eave at these cells or leave them as chimney masonry.

Not refused, but overwritten: the chimney's own cuts through the ell and body eaves (32,3,15 lintel, 32,5,15, 32,10,15 and the owner's 91,11,15 etc.) replace earlier parts' blocks silently. runParts' guard does not treat those cells as owned, so they never show in REFUSED. The lead should decide whether that is intended (flue walls through roofs, as the chimney comment says) and whether the guard should cover roof cells.

Warning from this part, not in the requested fixes, left alone: flight 'the landing at 86,7,9 has no headroom' (owner flight, z 14 to 10). Needs a look at the upper landing and the balcony/porch cells in fittings.
The hard-coded EAVE_KEPT list in hearths.mjs is a stopgap: if the roofs part changes its eave cells, the list must be updated to match.

waste.what: Worked out which cells of the chimney stacks collide with the roof by reading the refusal report and the built grid one cell at a time (a probe script for each coordinate, then a block-by-block check of kept cells).
waste.cost: About 6 full make.sh runs and 3 probe scripts, including one wrong attempt: a snapshot of every non-air cell that kept too many cells, because the guard only refuses cells owned by earlier parts.
waste.tool: A runParts/parts report option that lists, before the chimney runs, which cells are owned by earlier parts (or a dry-run mode that prints each part's would-be refusals with the owning part's name). mcd fit's roof-tiles-walling-the-flue check run at build time would have pointed at the three cells directly.

waste.what: Chimney stacks are called directly and overwrite whatever is in their cells, so any roof cell in the flue's path becomes an unreported write unless someone guards it by hand.
waste.cost: One design question and one extra make.sh run to confirm the three refused cells were the only true conflicts.
waste.tool: chimney() option such as keep: 'earlier' or avoid: [cells], so the library itself skips earlier parts' cells and returns them as refused, the same way vocab/h3.mjs chimney does (all-or-nothing) but per cell.

companions.task: Cut the barn's back eave at (65,13,15) and the owner's hip eave at (90,9,16) and (92,9,16) so the flue passes through as chimney masonry, not roof stairs or slabs; check the eave still closes against the stack.
Confirm the flue walls read as solid masonry through the three roof cells once the roof yields, and that the band course under the top is right on the owner's and barn's stacks.
